findings.claim: When the formatted type carries MessagePack attributes, they are ignored, which misses the acceptance criterion "If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured". With no SurrogateType, the collector always takes the contractless path (`CreateContractlessMembers`). It never inspects `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key]`, `[IgnoreMember]`, `[DataContract]`, `[DataMember]` or `[IgnoreDataMember]` on T. So a T marked `[MessagePackObject]` with `[Key(0)]` and `[IgnoreMember]` gets a string-keyed map that includes the ignored member. Per the maintainer comment, contractless mode should apply only when T has no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]`.

receipt_plan.detail: Run tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/GeneratedFormatterHonoursAttributesTests.cs. MessagePackObjectIgnoreMemberIsHonoured and DataContractIgnoreDataMemberIsHonoured both fail on head, because the generated TaggedFormatter source references the ignored member 'Secret'.

findings.claim: This hunk is unrelated to the requirement and corrupts timestamp data. The timestamp32 branch now tests `(data64 & 0x00000000ffffffffL) == 0` instead of the upper 32 bits. Values whose low 32 seconds bits are zero (e.g. the Unix epoch plus non-zero nanoseconds, or seconds = 2^32) are written as a 4-byte timestamp32, which drops the nanoseconds and the high seconds bits. Every ordinary whole-second DateTime that used to encode as timestamp32 now encodes as timestamp64, changing the wire bytes.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize DateTime values with base-built and head-built MessagePack and compare the bytes: `new DateTime(2020,1,1,0,0,0,DateTimeKind.Utc)` gives d6 ff (6 bytes) on base and d7 ff on head. Then round-trip `DateTime.UnixEpoch.AddTicks(1)` on head: the deserialized value loses its nanoseconds, so it is not equal to the input.

findings.claim: The contractless member set excludes public get-only properties and readonly fields, and constructor parameters are never matched. The existing contractless behaviour (ContractlessStandardResolver, L3) serializes public readable members and populates them via a matching constructor. So a T with get-only properties, or with only a parameterized constructor, is either silently not serialized or rejected. The requirement asks for "contractless behaviour over public members".

receipt_plan.detail: Define a referenced type `public class P { public P(int id){Id=id;} public int Id { get; } }`. Serialize it with ContractlessStandardResolver and with the generated formatter, and compare: the dynamic resolver writes {"Id":..}, while the generated formatter is rejected (MsgPack007/no ctor) or would write an empty map.

questions.text: For [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] in contractless mode, should public get-only properties and readonly fields of T be serialized (and deserialized via a matching constructor), as ContractlessStandardResolver does?
options: Yes, match ContractlessStandardResolver: include public readable members and match constructor parameters
No, only public read-write members with a parameterless constructor are in scope
questions.why_it_matters: If yes, the read-write-only filter and the missing constructor matching are a medium requirement gap. If no, the change's documented limitation is acceptable and the finding is dropped.
